utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session. Madam Registrar, can you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Counsel. For the Prosecution, Chester Stamp and Ekkehard Withopf, together with Kimberly Fleming as the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Appearances for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, Mirna Milanovic and Stephane Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Mr. Rodney Dixon, Mr. Ibrisimovic, and Mr. Nermin Mulalic, legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. The Chamber greets all of you, the Prosecution, the Defence, the accused, the interpreters, and all of those who enable this procedure. I would like to remind you that today we have to finish by 11.30 because there is another trial that starts at noon. So at 11.30 we shall finish, and we will adjourn until tomorrow morning at 9.00. And our last sitting this week will be on Friday. Can you please plan your schedule accordingly. On Friday, we have to finish with the last witness, and make sure you bear that in mind. I would like to ask the Defence, both Defence counsel, to tell me by Thursday at 9.00, after having heard the requests of the Prosecution, with regard to the submissions, I would like to know what the Defence thinks about it no later than Thursday at 9.00. It would be very good if we could render a decision before Friday so that the Appeals Chamber could then deal on the issue, since this is a very important issue for our further proceedings. That's why I would kindly ask the Defence to submit their opinion, if they object to the written submission by the Prosecution. I know that you have a lot of work to do, but we have to render our decisions fast. These decisions can also be rendered in January and/or in February. However, every time the Defence gets up on their feet and say we don't want that Prosecution to use the written document, then we have to deal with that. So if there are no other matters to discuss, we will continue with the witness examination. First of all, let's move into closed session. Can you please check, Madam Registrar, whether we are in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a witness who does not require protective measures, as far as I understand. So we have an hour. I don't think we'll have time to finish. So he will have to come back tomorrow. Could the usher please bring the usher in -- the witness in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Witness. Can you hear the interpretation of what I am saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you tell me your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Dragan Rados.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 10th of November, 1959.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which city were you born in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the village of Brdo, Lasva.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your current profession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a pool attendant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where do you live at the moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I live in the USA, in Florida, Orlando.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you have arrived from the USA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't hear that very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have arrived, you have come here from the USA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What sort of status do you have in the USA? Are you an American resident? Do you have a green card, or are you a tourist there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am now an American citizen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are an American citizen. You're going to testify before this Tribunal now, and you must now make the solemn declaration. The usher will show you the text you have to read. Could you please read it out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You can sit down. Witness, you are going to answer the questions put to you by the Prosecution. You will then be cross-examined by the Defence. And if necessary, the Prosecution will re-examine you. As we have to conclude this hearing at 11.30, unfortunately you will have to return tomorrow morning. The Prosecution may commence its examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness will focus his testimony on the killing of Zvonko Rajic and the treatment in the Zenica Music School.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Rados. Mr. Rados, have you ever been a member of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber from when to when.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: From 1980 to 1981.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Have you ever been a member of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber as to when you joined the HVO.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date. Perhaps in April, May, or June 1992

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And of which unit have you been a member of?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: It was the Lasva local commune.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And where was this unit based?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: In Lasva.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: In the Lasva area, members of what ethnicities used to live in the Lasva area, end of 1992 and beginning of 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: The Croats, Serbs, and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Which ethnic group has been in the majority at the end of 1992 and the beginning of 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: The Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And which group has been the next biggest group?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: Probably the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Having been a member of the HVO, what was your position in the HVO at the beginning of 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: I was a squad leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And who has been your commander at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: Zvonko Rajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: The situation in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you've been asked to approach the microphones a bit, since the booths are having a little difficulty. Please approach the microphones. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: The situation in the Lasva Valley area end of 1992-1993, can you please describe for the Trial Chamber what the situation has been about.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: The population of the Lasva area did not trust each other very much during that period. There was tension.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you go in more detail in respect to the tensions that existed in January 1993 in the Lasva area.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: Well, because of the relations in the -- at the time, because of the incidents that occurred in the Lasva Valley, the tension was quite great.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: You informed the Trial Chamber that you were born in Brdo. Where were you living in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: In Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Did there come a time in January 1993 when the village of Brdo was attacked?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber when this happened.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: That happened in the second half of January, early in the morning

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: In the second half of January 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber who the attackers were.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: The BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: At that day, in the second half of January 1993, can you please describe for the Trial Chamber what happened.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: It was early in the morning. I was sleeping at home. I was woken by the sound of shooting. Shots appeared to be coming from all directions. You could mostly hear infantry weapons, but there were also a few louder explosions. I don't know how long this lasted. I know that it was dark when I woke up, and after a certain period of time it was daytime when I heard some voices. Someone was calling my name out. And I recognised my wife's voice. She called out my name and she said that we should surrender, that we should go outside, and that they wouldn't do anything to us. She said they wouldn't touch us and that it was necessary for them to stop shooting. I went outside with a rifle and headed in the direction of my former house, my old house. I noticed a significant number of BH army troops who were in the area, and they all pointed their rifles at me. I told them not to shoot, and I was holding my rifle in my hands. I got as far as my old house. A BH army soldier was lying in front of my old house. I approached the soldier and said -- but I noticed that he had blood on him -- if someone wants to help me, which one BH army member did, I suggested we should take him to the main road, so that he could be treated, so that they could offer him -- provide him with first aid. We took him to the road. A car was supposed to arrive to collect him and take him to the nearest hospital so that he could be treated there. While carrying the soldier, I didn't notice any signs of -- signs that he was alive. And then with some of the Muslim BH army soldiers I continued to the water reservoir which supplied the village with water. There were quite a few BH army soldiers up there. My wife was also there, and quite a lot of people from Dusina had formed a group.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: May I interrupt at this point in time, Mr. Rados. You were saying that there were quite a significant number of ABiH army troops. Can you give the Trial Chamber a rough estimate about the numbers.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: In front of my old house, at the side and towards Blasko's house, on the slope and around the reservoir there were probably more than 50 of them. They were also in the rear towards Potcimalj [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Do you know who has been in charge of these members of the ABiH, in charge at the time at the spot in Brdo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: I'm not sure I have understood your question very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: I'm asking you about your impression who has been in charge of the attacking soldiers of -- attacking soldiers of the ABiH at the time. With whom did you talk to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: There was an ABiH army soldier there. I started speaking to him. I suggested - and he also suggested - that the shooting wasn't necessary, that it should stop and that discussions should be held. He accepted this, and he suggested that I should go from the other side, since that was the Vranica Hill there, and the HVO soldiers were there, he suggested that I should go and tell them and that I should find a place where we could negotiate, have discussions. My wife and I went to Vranjaca [phoen]. I saw Zvonko Rajic there and I told him that it had to stop, that I had already spoken to them, and that he should come and reach an agreement with the BH army soldier and see how this problem could be solved. We came to an agreement. I don't know exactly how many times my wife and I went there. But the agreement was that we should meet in my house and that they should talk there. After a certain period of time, this is what took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And who was talking to whom in your house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: Zvonko Rajic was talking to a BH army soldier. The agreement was -- well, all those soldiers, this was the first time I'd seen them. And Zvonko didn't know them either. They started talking about putting an end to the shooting and about him going to the local commune and finding representatives of the BH army from Lasva. And they were to start talking in order to solve the problem. The agreement was that the HVO soldiers and the ABiH soldiers should be split into two groups and they should be mixed up and go to the Lasva local commune in order to start talks there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Right. Do you know an individual with the name Edin Hakanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: Yes. He was with us. He was with us in my house. I think he went with me to Vranjaca and back on the last occasion to tell BH army soldiers that an agreement had been reached and that they should come to my house and start talking there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: What was Mr. Edin Hakanovic's role during the negotiations in your house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: We didn't speak very much. Zvonko Rajic and another BH army soldier were trying to reach an agreement. They were talking, and we observed them from the side. Zvonko spoke on a couple of occasions. I'm not quite sure what he said to Edin Hakanovic, but we decided that we should all go to Lasva and be mixed up in two groups in order to continue with the talks in Lasva.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: A few minutes ago, Mr. Rados, you said that the BiH army -- members of the ABiH came with civilians from Dusina. Can you describe for the Trial Chamber the concrete situation in respect to the civilians from Dusina.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: When I reached the reservoir which supplied the water, I don't know whether all the inhabitants were up there or almost all the inhabitants, but there were a lot of them. They were at one side and they were surrounded by ABiH soldiers. I was speaking with my wife -- I spoke to my wife, and she said that they didn't come here on a voluntary basis. She said that they had to come there and she said that two soldiers had been killed in Dusina and two men had been wounded and that they had been used as human shields.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. Rados, you were just telling us that after the negotiations in your house, the group of HVO soldiers was divided into two groups. Can you inform the Trial Chamber in which group you have been.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: I was in a group in which there were also BH army soldiers. The main road to Lasva was used. The other group went over Vranjaca via the relay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Was Zvonko Rajic in your group?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Whilst you were being escorted by ABiH soldiers, what did Zvonko Rajic do?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: I don't quite understand this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Whilst you were walking and escorted by the ABiH soldiers, did anything happen to Zvonko Rajic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: We were heading in the direction of Lasva. We arrived more or less in front of Hazim Hakanovic's house. At that point someone said that we couldn't continue. One of the BH army soldiers said so, because there were some sort of ambush lower down and he said we had to return, we had to go back. Zvonko Rajic said that there was no one down below, that there wasn't an ambush, that they shouldn't be afraid, that we would go to the local commune. He said we should go to the local commune and continue with the talks down there. They then agreed that Mijo Ljubicic and a BH soldier should go in front of us in the direction of Lasva to check that there was no one down below, and the ABiH soldier suggested that we should return. At first we didn't want to, but it seemed as if we had no other choice and we started turning back. We got to the crossroads leading towards Dusina and Brdo, and after about 20 to 30 metres ABiH soldiers jumped aside and pointed their rifles at us and said that we should throw our weapons down. In fact, at the time I didn't have my weapon on me. I had left it in front of my old house when I saw the soldier who had been killed there. They then took the weapons. They had already started pushing us around. There were threats, and they'd ask us "Why did it have to all come to this," et cetera. They started turning back. They went in front of us -- we went in front of them. And they followed us up to Barucija's house. At that point Zvonko Rajic stood aside and he started fleeing in the opposite direction. One of the BH army soldiers reacted. He fired a few shots, I don't know how many exactly. I know that I couldn't see Zvonko any more, but I heard him groaning and it seemed as if he had been hit. They ordered one of us to go to fetch him, since he couldn't walk. I don't remember who went, but they brought him back and I noticed that he had been wounded in the leg. They told us to carry him and to take the route that we had come by.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: May I interrupt you --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: To go back where we had come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Who was told to carry him? Were you amongst the ones that were told to carry him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: While Zvonko was being carried back -- well, as he was quite heavy, the people who were carrying him changed. And at some location before my old house, there was a big pear tree there. We put Zvonko down so that he could rest or to change the people who were carrying him. I can't remember exactly. At that point a group of BH army soldiers were approaching from the opposite direction. In fact, they were running towards us. When they arrived, some of them started hitting Zvonko. It didn't last very long. One of the soldiers who had arrived took a weapon out. It had a short barrel, and he shot Zvonko. It was an automatic weapon. I noticed that while he was shooting from this weapon someone else tried to hit him, and I know that one BH army soldier was hit on that occasion in the leg or the toes, in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. Rados, when Zvonko Rajic was shot by the ABiH soldier, how far away had you been at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: Between a metre and a half and 2 metres, not more than that. A metre, a metre and a half, or 2 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Where on his body did the ABiH soldier shoot Zvonko Rajic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: In this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please describe for the record what the area is about in words, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: The area of the chest, near the neck. It was a burst of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: "A burst of fire," does this mean that the ABiH soldier from his automatic weapon shot a number of bullets, and do you have a rough idea how many bullets he shot?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: The weapon that the BH army soldier had was an automatic weapon with a short barrel. Later on I heard that it was some kind of automatic weapon with a short barrel called a Skorpion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Zvonko Rajic, was he still alive after he had been shot in the area of his chest of his body?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: No, he wasn't. He didn't show any signs of life. I think that he was dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: At that point --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: At that point, the BH army soldier still had the weapon in his hand. He was still holding the weapon. I approached him and said that he didn't have to fire any more shots and that I could tell him everything that he wanted to know. The first question he asked me was, "Where is the VBR, the multiple rocket launcher?"

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. Rados, may I interrupt you here. Do you know the ABiH soldier who shot Zvonko Rajic? Do you know him by name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: I had never seen that BH army soldier before, and at the time I didn't know his name. I was subsequently told that his last name was Patkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Who did tell you that his last name was Patkovic and when have you been told that his last name was Patkovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: I'm not sure who told me, but this was the name on everyone's lips. This is what I heard after we had left Zenica or perhaps in Zenica, or maybe after I had left Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: After you had left Zenica, what's the exact time you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: That was perhaps two or three weeks after the event.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: After the murder of Zvonko Rajic, where did you go to, escorted by the ABiH soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: After that, they tied our hands and we set off in the direction of Zenica, in the direction opposite to the one we had taken the first time. Towards Zenica, to the estuary of the Lasva river, to the point where the Lasva River joins the Bosna River.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: At this point in time, did you still have your military jacket?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: After Zvonko had been killed, they took the upper parts of our uniform off, all our clothing off. They took our jackets. They took what they liked. I think they had taken Zvonko's jacket earlier on. I don't know when exactly. It was probably immediately afterwards, and when they first told us that we should surrender our weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: What did the ABiH soldiers do with your military uniform jackets?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: They took some of them. I know that they didn't want mine, because it was old. And a BH army soldier threw my glasses on the ground and stomped on them, thus destroying them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: You just told the Trial Chamber that your and the other HVO soldiers' hands were tied up. Who gave the order? Who was the person in charge at this time within the ABiH soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: I think the soldier who killed Zvonko Rajic was Patkovic, and he also issued an order for us to be tied, for our hands to be tied with the ropes that were in our jackets. And that's how they took us to the confluence of the River Lasva with the Bosna River.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Once you arrived at the River Lasva, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: When we arrived down there, there was a big group of BH army soldiers there. I saw them getting in and out. And one soldier of the BH army, a heavily built man, singled me out and started to do like he would beat me. He was shoving me around, pushed me towards the wall, and at the same time another younger soldier arrived. He was carrying a pistol. And he put the pistol against my forehead. At that moment I saw Hazim Barucija. He was also a BH army member. He was from Lasva. This all lasted very short. Then they put us on buses and took us all the way to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: May I interrupt you here. You were just telling the Trial Chamber that in Lasva there was a big group of ABiH members. Can you detail the units to the best of your recollection which such soldiers belonged to.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: I did not know any of these soldiers. They were unknown to me. Later on I heard that they were the Zeljeznicki Battalion and the MOS.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber for what MOS stands for.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: I think it is the Muslim armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: You were just telling the Trial Chamber that you were taken into buses. Did you voluntarily go into such buses, you and the other HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: No. Some were saying that we were supposed to go to a penitentiary and the others were saying that we were to go to another bus. I didn't know at the time where we were being taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: At this point in time, were your hands still tied up?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Were the hands of the other HVO soldiers still tied up?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: In the buses, have you been escorted by ABiH soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: Yes. There were not many of them, but there were still some on the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Where were you brought to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: From Lasva, across the Lasva Bridge, we took the main road to Zenica, and we entered straight from the buses into the building which was very close to the Zenica park. I could notice that. And most probably we were taken to the first floor. There were some benches there. They looked like students' benches, benches where pupils sit. That's where we were lined up and we sat down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: May I interrupt you here. This building you were brought to, does this building have a name and did it have a name at the point in time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: It was the music school. That's what everybody called it. I don't know whether it was actually the music school, but everybody called the building the music school.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Once you have been brought in the building which everybody called the music school, what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: We got in. We were put in a room where students' benches were. When we sat down, I don't know exactly whether this happened before or after -- in any case, a few minutes later a soldier of the ABiH came in and slapped each and every one of us. And after that, they untied us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: After a soldier of the ABiH had slapped each of you, what happened then and after you have been untied?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: People were leaving one by one. I was the last one who was supposed to leave that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And do you know where these people were brought to once they were made leaving the room?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: They were most probably taken for some sort of interrogation. I only noticed as they were coming back to the room it looked by the way they walked and by the way that they behaved that they were -- they had been beaten up. Some of them even said that they had been beaten up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Were you also taken for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: What happened to you during the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: A soldier of the ABiH escorted me up the stairs from that room, maybe to the second floor. But I'm not sure about the floor. And then somewhere midway another soldier hit me on the back with his rifle butt. We entered a room in which a man was sitting. He had a military uniform on. He may have been 30 to 40. He had dark hair, dark beard. And while the door was being closed behind me, the soldier who had escorted me hit me with his rifle butt on the back. I told him to stop. I told him, "Whatever I know and whatever you may be interested in, I'll tell you." And then he did not beat me any more, and then the person whom I found sitting in that room started asking me questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Have you been beaten in the presence of the person who was asking you questions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: No. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: After the interrogation had finished, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: Then another soldier of the ABiH took me to another room. This room looked like a lunchroom, like a place where you could take your meals. The soldier who was there hit me again, this time in the neck. I don't know what he used to hit me, whether it was his rifle or some other wooden implement. I told him as well that there was no need for them to beat me, because I was willing to tell them whatever I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Once you were hit by this soldier, after that what happened to you and what happened to the other HVO soldiers which were brought with you to the building which was known as the Zenica Music School?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: After the interrogation, we were transferred to the basement of the same building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: In this basement of the same building, were there already any other people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: There were three soldiers there, three men who were members of the HVO from Drivusa who had been brought in the night before, as far as I know. They were frightened, very edgy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Once you were brought in this room, what happened to you and the other group of HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly whether this happened the same night or the following night, but in any case two soldiers came during the night and they brought some lists with them. They read out the names on those lists with the names of Viktor Rajic and my name on one of the lists. And they said to all the others that they should face the wall with their hands on the back and they started beating Viktor Rajic. He was beaten, kicked, I don't know for how long. But they stopped when he started bleeding profusely from somewhere on his face.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Sorry, may I just interrupt you here. These soldiers who were beating him, what army did they belong to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADOS
utterances.text: It was very hard to tell. I know that one of them had boots on, and the other one had trainers. One of them was taller, and another one was shorter. The shorter guy wore a balaclava, so you could only see his eyes. Once they stopped hitting Viktor, they started beating me. They kicked me. They hit me in the rib area. They were not satisfied, and one of them took the rope from the jacket. He tied my two thumbs together behind my back very high up and tied one end of the rope around my neck. And they took a wooden object which looked like a baseball bat and they started hitting me with that bat in the rib area. I don't know how long this may have lasted or how many times I was hit. They stopped when they heard a loud noise. And after that, I was only kicked once by the man who was wearing trainers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. Rados, we'll stop at this point in time. And I will continue your examination tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for -- to the Prosecution for having noticed that it was half past 11.00. Witness, I'm afraid you have to return tomorrow at quarter to 9.00, because we shall resume at 9.00. Hopefully -- we were supposed to work until quarter to 2.00; however, we have to be out of this courtroom because another trial is about to start at 12.00. I would kindly ask the usher to take the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are adjourned until 9.00 tomorrow morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 17th day of December, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.32 a.m.,
